claim.title: Isotropic Min-Norm Risk Formula
claim.statement: For the isotropic linear model (Sigma = I) with i.i.d. features, the asymptotic prediction risk of the min-norm least squares estimator is R(γ) = σ²/(γ(1-γ)) for γ < 1 and R(γ) = r²(1 - 1/γ) + σ²/(γ - 1) for γ > 1, where r² = ||β||² and γ = p/n.
claim.test_plan: Simulate n=1000, p=γn for γ in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1.1, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0]. Generate X ~ N(0, I_p), y = Xβ + ε with β fixed norm r=1, ε ~ N(0, 1). Compute min-norm solution β_hat = X^T(X X^T)^{-1}y. Estimate risk on 10,000 test points. Compare empirical risk to theoretical formula. Pass if relative error < 5% for all γ.
claim.success_criterion: Empirical risk matches theoretical formula within 5% relative error for all tested γ values.

feedback: Transferred from the arxiv-1912.07242 audit round: Monte-Carlo audits at d=1000 timed out 3x within the 20-min bound; d<=300 (T<=300 trials, focused grids around critical points) gave statistically clean verdicts in minutes. Design for that envelope. Asymptotic closed-forms converge quickly in d — a large-d run is wasted budget, not better evidence.
